messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HOSTED-RUNTIME us-east-1 - KV_CACHE_OOM spike detected in continuous-batching pool (severity: P0). 30% of nodes reporting OOMs in last 5m. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/kvcache-oom

alex: acked, oncall here. grabbing metrics and current rollout config.

amelia: @alex FYI saw elevated long prompt tail from a customer in us-east in the last hour — might be correlated.

alex: copying logs + quick snapshot, running `redwoodctl runtime inspect --pool hosted-us-east --filter kvcache`

alex: log excerpt:
```\n2026-03-15T01:02:12Z ERROR kvcache: eviction failed: unable to free pages: memory=126GB used=128GB
2026-03-15T01:02:13Z ERROR runtime: batch-window flush failure: oom allocating KV shard
2026-03-15T01:02:14Z WARN  continuous-batching: window_ms increased to 300ms by rollout policy
```

maria: ok so batch window auto-tuned to 300ms in recent rollout, that increases prefix caching footprint on long contexts. could cause blowup if customers send 100k token prompts.

sam: @alex can we quickly toggle prefetch+continuous-batching off for hosted-us-east while we triage? prefer a config flip vs restarting nodes.

alex: proposing hotfix:
```
redwoodctl runtime update-config --pool hosted-us-east \
  --set kvcache.eviction_policy=aggressive \
  --set continuous_batch.window_ms=50 \
  --set kvcache.max_seq_length=2048 \
  --set kvcache.prefetch=false
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: config-change accepted: change-id=chg_8f3a, rolling to 10% -> 100% over 5m.

alex: rolled to 100% at 01:06Z. watching memory and error rates.

lina: customers impacted list from metrics: ~0.6% of total requests in us-east returned 5xx between 00:58-01:05Z. Top 3 tenants by error volume: tenant-a (44%), tenant-b (18%), internal-eval-suite (12%). cc @cs-bot to surface to CS.

cs-bot: @cs-team alert: tenant-a experienced elevated 5xx from 00:58-01:10Z. Suggested message: "We experienced transient inference errors due to cache memory pressure; mitigation is in place and we are monitoring. Will follow up with root cause and timeline."

maria: immediate telemetry after change: host memory usage dropped from ~95% -> ~62% across affected pool within 90s. Error rate decreased to baseline by 01:08Z. Good signal.

sam: nice. we should still add a protective guard: reject requests with token_length > 50k for hosted runtime for now. can't silently accept runaway contexts.

alex: agree. adding request-limiter flag now.
```
redwoodctl runtime update-config --pool hosted-us-east --set request_limits.max_tokens=50000
```
Applied.

maria: quick follow-up checks: p99 latency slightly increased (~20ms) due to smaller batches but acceptable compared to OOM. No active degradation of throughput.

lina: filing impact summary to incident tracker. Estimated customer sessions errored: ~1.2k in 12m window. No SLA breaches yet, flag for postmortem.

alex: action items while hot:
- keep continuous-batching window at 50ms for next 4h
- schedule canary rollback for any other recent rollout that touched batching logic (rollout ids: r-2026-03-14-02)
- collect top 50 longest prompts and correlate to tenants
- create temporary traffic route rule to shift heavy token customers to dedicated if they opt-in

lina: added to tracker: INC-2001234567. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml to review kernel selection for long-context quantized models.

maria: handing off to @maria for next shift at 04:00Z. leaving runbook notes and commands executed in the incident doc.

maria: (oncall takeover) I'm in. repeating checks. memory stable. starting root cause triage: looks like combined effect of a recent batching rollout + a small set of tenants sending multi-segment long prompts that triggered aggressive prefetch.

sam: follow-up hypothesis: auto-tuner increased window_ms to favor throughput during low load; it didn't account for tail distribution of prompt lengths. we need a tuner guard for max_kv_footprint or per-tenant limits.

alex: agreed. I'll open a RFC to add memory-aware tuner cap and per-tenant prefetch throttle. assigning to eng-runtime.

cs-bot: CS outreach queued for tenant-a and tenant-b. template message ready for approval.

ops-bot: incident resolved signal: system metrics stable for 45m and error rate returned to baseline. closing alert in 2h if no regression.

maria: leaving notes for postmortem: timeline, commands executed, customer impact numbers, mitigation tradeoffs (latency vs. stability). tagging @sam and @alex to draft root cause.

alex: drafting short postmortem, will include proposed mitigations: 1) add memory cap to auto-tuner, 2) per-tenant prefetch throttles, 3) better canary for batching window changes, 4) automatic reject for >50k token requests on hosted.

lina: thanks all. close loop with CS after postmortem.

maria: handing off to night oncall @sam at 08:00Z. if anything spikes re-open pager. :wave:

sam: got it, thanks. monitoring alerts set to stricter thresholds.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager closed (auto) - no active alerts. incident status: mitigated.
